statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Every published hour falls inside the scheduled weekend closure of CME equity-index futures and the NAS100 CFD, so no pathological price path can form; the macro backdrop behind Stress remains difficult and unresolved.
recommendation: Tail is held well below the block threshold for the full window because Nasdaq-100 venues are shut until Sunday 22:00Z, which is past the final published slot. Stress is retained in the elevated band as a description of the long-end yield, energy and inflation-expectation backdrop rather than of any in-window exposure.
headline: Nasdaq-100 in scheduled weekend closure after an orderly Friday finish; Tail at its floor, Stress elevated on yields and energy
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed Friday at 30,608.14, up 0.42%, inside a contained 30,413.59-30,667.56 range and roughly 60 points below the session high, so the observed path showed no persistent one-way structure, no shallow-pullback signature and no session-extreme holding. Breadth was supportive rather than narrow: the Dow added 0.93%, the S&P 500 0.51% and the Nasdaq Composite about 0.5%, and all three notched weekly gains. VIX eased 5.1% to 14.87, and WTI settled near $92.4, down 2.3%, with Brent near $104.4, down 2.1%, after Iran publicly proposed a seven-day sequence to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for the US lifting its naval blockade, waiving oil sanctions and observing a ceasefire. That relief sits against a genuinely stressed backdrop: the 30-year Treasury yield reached its highest level since 2004 during the week and the 10-year a 19-year high near 5.23%, H.15 recorded 4.87% at 2 years and 5.18% at 10 years on 24 September, final September University of Michigan sentiment fell to 48.1 with year-ahead inflation expectations at 4.6% versus 4.0%, and Brent is still up roughly 17% on the month with the blockade unresolved. CME equity-index futures settled for the week at 21:00Z and do not reopen until Sunday 22:00Z, beyond the last published forecast slot, so every hour in this assessment lies inside a scheduled halt. Tail is therefore held near its floor: sustained mean-reversion failure requires a tradable price path, and none exists. Stress stays elevated because the yield and energy regime is unresolved and will be tested next week by August PCE on Wednesday, ISM Manufacturing on Thursday and the September employment report on Friday. The principal conditional risk is gap formation at the Sunday reopen if weekend Hormuz diplomacy advances or collapses; that will be scored on the observed path once trading resumes rather than anticipated here. Shared Finviz context was read but was both stale, collected 18:58Z, and partial, with its futures and calendar sections unavailable, so it was not used as evidence.

lookbackSummary: Across the trailing 24 hours the published Claude state stayed between Tail 12 and 22, alternating green and yellow and never reaching the block threshold. Overnight and early European hours held Tail at 17-20 in normal or mixed conditions, three trend-up prints appeared between 06:00Z and 11:00Z as the index worked higher, and the US afternoon settled back to 18-19 in mixed conditions into the cash close. The 13:00Z hour has no published assessment and is marked unavailable. Stress held a narrow 54-59 band for most of the period before easing to 50 in the final hour as venues closed for the weekend.
outlookSummary: The entire published window falls inside the scheduled CME weekend closure: futures settled at 21:00Z on Friday and do not reopen until Sunday 22:00Z, past the final slot. Tail is held between 9 and 11 across all 24 hours because sustained mean-reversion failure requires a tradable price path. Stress eases from 49 toward 45 through the quiet overnight and Saturday hours and firms back to 50 into the end of the window as unpriced weekend headline flow accumulates ahead of the reopen. Confidence decays from 86 to 75 purely as the last verified Friday observation ages across the weekend gap. The mapped policy state stays EA_ON for every published slot. The main conditional risk, gap formation at the Sunday reopen driven by Hormuz diplomacy or a renewed long-end yield impulse, sits outside this window and will be scored on the observed path once trading resumes.
